component: Measured, adaptive MTP->ordinary park with memory that outlives a cohort (omlx #4112 port)
status: implemented, default OFF (mtp_ordinary_handoff.adaptive_park; kill switch MLX2_MTP_ADAPTIVE_PARK=0); unqualified. Static max_mtp_width stays the default for every adapter.

sources.source_pr: jundot/omlx#4112 (perf(mtp): stop shared MTP from slowing down busy batches), open at read time
source_regions: batch_policy.py: _CLEAR_LOSS, BatchPolicy.observe losing/clear_losing streaks, should_park, park, start_parked, held_up, ParkMemory (seed/parked/retired)
sources.not_ported: prompt_priming.py batched priming folds (draft-head history fold batching): mlx2's self-MTP lanes have no per-step priming fold on the ordinary path.

destination_paths: src/mlx2/runtime/generate.py (MTPGenerationBatch park_memory decision/peek; BatchGenerator _build_mtp_park_memory, _observe_park_round, adaptive latch release)
src/mlx2/prometheus.py (mtp_adaptive_park_* and new handoff reason counters)
modifications: omlx parks within a cohort (ordinary decode inside the shared-MTP batch, re-measured after a cooldown); mlx2's handoff is one-way per lane (the cohort migrates to the ordinary batcher). A 'park' here is that handoff; re-measurement happens on a later cohort after the verdict's cooldown expires.

omlx scores expected tokens per ms per draft depth from modelled acceptance and per-depth call costs; mlx2 measures realised tokens per wall interval between two consecutive pure decode rounds of the same kind and width (MTP rounds that completed a proposal; ordinary-only rounds), with no prompt work queued, so MTP and ordinary share one timing domain. Mixed rounds are skipped and counted.
Verdict keyed by cohort width (omlx: row count of the uid cohort); a verdict at k parks cohorts of width >= k; a cohort ahead for 32 decisions clears verdicts at <= its width (same rule).
Clear loss < 0.9x for 4 decisions and sustained loss <= 1.03x for 16 decisions kept from omlx; decisions count only fresh MTP samples, not every boundary.
Cooldown counted in ordinary decode steps (128 doubling to 4096, as omlx); on expiry the MTP rate at and above that width is dropped so the next cohort re-measures from scratch.

New: where ordinary decode was never measured at a width, the rate measured at the nearest wider width bounds it from below (step time is non-decreasing in width); with no ordinary evidence at all, the static max_mtp_width decides (cold start).
New: the ordinary-handoff latch releases when one more arrival would not be parked (static: plain width < max_mtp_width).
Memory registry keyed by (model object via weakref, route config hash, static width, settings), so it outlives BatchGenerator rebuilds as well as cohorts.
Default off, kill switch, bounded counters, receipt evidence (reason, rule, rates, ratio, verdict width) per handed-off lane.
validation: CPU: tests/test_mtp_park_memory.py, 25 tests (settings/refusals, clear and sustained loss, bound, verdict outlives cohort and parks wider widths only, hold clears, cooldown expiry and doubling, registry, BatchGenerator integration on a tiny Qwen4 incl. exact handoff vs ordinary greedy, kill switch). GPU A/B (M5 Max, 2026-10-02): Flash-Next 2/3/4/8/16 lanes vs static width 3, 4 alternated reps: parked cohorts match static and are token-identical; each probe cohort costs 5-8% at 8/16 lanes; no width found where MTP beats the static boundary. Details: qualification/runs/port-park-memory-20261002/README.md.
